title: Janapada of Magadha
capsule: Magadha was one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas of Iron Age northern India, centered on Rajagriha (modern Rajgir) in the lower Gangetic plain of Bihar, and attested from around 600 BCE. Under the Haryanka dynasty, kings Bimbisara (c. 543–492 BCE) and his son Ajatashatru (c. 492–460 BCE) aggressively expanded Magadha, annexing neighboring Anga and clashing with the Vajjika League; both rulers were contemporaries and patrons of the Buddha and Mahavira. The kingdom's social structure notably elevated Kshatriyas above Brahmins, diverging from Vedic orthodoxy, and the region served as the nursery for the later Nanda and Maurya pan-Indian empires. By 500 BCE Magadha had emerged as the dominant power in the Gangetic basin, a trajectory that would culminate in Chandragupta Maurya's empire two centuries later.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territory around Rajagriha is well-supported by Buddhist and Jain sources and archaeological finds at Rajgir, but precise political boundaries for the 600–500 BCE period remain inferential.
